title: Psychology’s influence on our digital world (SOP32)

sentences.en: As a podcast listener, you may already be integrated in the world of media technology, but psychologists are continuously trying to figure out how and why people use devices like
sentences.zh: 作为播客听众，你可能已经融入了媒体科技的世界，但心理学家一直在试图弄清楚人们是如何以及为什么要使用诸如

sentences.en: smartphones or activity trackers.
sentences.zh: 智能手机或活动追踪器之类的设备的。

sentences.en: These devices monitor our moods, our activity, and they can spur more engagement with others.
sentences.zh: 这些设备监测我们的情绪、活动，并且它们能激发我们与他人更多的互动。

sentences.en: In this episode, we speak with one psychologist who applies psychological science to interactive and mobile media technology, an area of research
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们采访了一位将心理学科学应用于互动和移动媒体技术的心理学家，这一研究领域

sentences.en: that is constantly changing as the platforms become more sophisticated and much more interactive.
sentences.zh: 随着平台变得越来越复杂、互动性越来越强而不断变化。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton, and this is Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿，这里是《心理学话语》。

sentences.en: Pamela Rutledge is director of the Media Psychology Research Center, and she teaches and designs media psychology courses at Fielding Graduate University.
sentences.zh: 帕梅拉·拉特利奇是媒体心理学研究中心的主任，她在菲尔丁研究生大学教授并设计媒体心理学课程。

sentences.en: She is also active as a consultant, speaker, and researcher on applying psychological science to interactive technology and social media.
sentences.zh: 她还作为顾问、演讲者和研究员活跃在将心理学科学应用于互动技术和社交媒体的领域。

sentences.en: She is editor-in-chief of the online journal Media Psychology Review.
sentences.zh: 她是网络期刊《媒体心理学评论》的主编。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Rutledge.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，拉特利奇博士。

sentences.en: Oh, it's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 哦，很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: First of all, tell us a little bit about your area of expertise, which is media psychology.
sentences.zh: 首先，请跟我们谈谈您的专业领域，也就是媒体心理学。

sentences.en: What does a media psychologist do, and what do you do as director of the Media Psychology Research Center?
sentences.zh: 媒体心理学家是做什么的？作为媒体心理学研究中心的主任，您又做些什么？

sentences.en: Well, media psychology is fundamentally using the tools of psychology to think about media and technologies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，媒体心理学基本上就是利用心理学的工具来思考媒体和技术。

sentences.en: So it's really using that in an applied way.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实是以一种应用的方式来使用这些工具。

sentences.en: And at the Media Psychology Research Center, we work with a number of media projects applying the fundamentals of psychology to help companies
sentences.zh: 在媒体心理学研究中心，我们参与了许多媒体项目，将心理学的基础知识应用于帮助公司

sentences.en: and organizations and even individuals understand how to better design, develop, and teach about media and technology.
sentences.zh: 、组织甚至个人了解如何更好地设计、开发媒体和技术以及开展相关教学。

sentences.en: There's a lot of interest in how new technologies are affecting our behavior.
sentences.zh: 人们对新技术如何影响我们的行为有着极大的兴趣。

sentences.en: Steve here, one of the producers of the podcast, he wears his Fitbit every day.
sentences.zh: 我们的制作人之一史蒂夫，他每天都佩戴Fitbit。

sentences.en: I see you have one as well.
sentences.zh: 我看到你也有一个。

sentences.en: And he competes with other people to get the greatest number of steps.
sentences.zh: 他与其他人比赛，看谁走的步数最多。

sentences.en: So in a study of one, this would seem to indicate he's improving his health with this technology.
sentences.zh: 所以对个人的一项研究表明，这似乎表明他正在通过这项技术改善自己的健康。

sentences.en: Is this something psychologists are studying or using to monitor people's behaviors and how so?
sentences.zh: 这是心理学家正在研究或用来监测人们行为的事情吗？如果是，是如何做到的？

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a lot of research going on right now, what we call the quantified self, where people are using wearable technologies to get information that they use to motivate
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，目前正在进行大量被称为量化自我的研究，人们使用可穿戴技术获取信息，并用这些信息来激励

sentences.en: themselves to make judgments about their performance.
sentences.zh: 自己对自己的表现做出判断。

sentences.en: But a really critical part of this is the social connection.
sentences.zh: 但其中一个非常关键的部分是社交连接。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of competition.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多竞争。

sentences.en: I wear the jawbone up, not the Fitbit, but my team includes my daughters.
sentences.zh: 我戴的是Jawbone Up，而不是Fitbit，但我的团队包括我的女儿们。

sentences.en: And so we're always comparing where did you walk?
sentences.zh: 所以我们总是互相比较，你走到哪儿了？

sentences.en: How much did you walk?
sentences.zh: 你走了多少路？

sentences.en: And it's really fun to get a yay mom after you've done some exercising.
sentences.zh: 在你做完一些运动后，听到一句“妈妈真棒”真的很有趣。

sentences.en: What about tracking people's moods, stepping away from the exercising, but to moods?
sentences.zh: 那如果抛开运动不谈，追踪人们的情绪呢？

sentences.en: Smartphones track people's movements.
sentences.zh: 智能手机会追踪人们的移动情况。

sentences.en: And some researchers at Northwestern University were able to show that people who moved less during the day were more depressed or could be more depressed.
sentences.zh: 西北大学的一些研究人员能够证明，白天活动较少的人更加抑郁，或者可能更容易抑郁。

sentences.en: How do you think smartphones are going to change how we track or monitor people's moods and mental health as we move forward?
sentences.zh: 随着未来的发展，您认为智能手机将如何改变我们追踪或监测人们情绪和心理健康的方式？

sentences.en: It won't just be smartphones that are changing.
sentences.zh: 发生改变的将不仅仅是智能手机。

sentences.en: I think that it's going to be a lot more integration of technology.
sentences.zh: 我认为这将是技术的更大融合。

sentences.en: We have to remember that there really isn't a separation between our mind and our body.
sentences.zh: 我们必须记住，我们的心灵和身体之间并没有真正意义上的分离。

sentences.en: So it makes perfect sense that we would start tracking mood in addition to our physical behavior.
sentences.zh: 因此，除了追踪我们的身体行为之外，我们开始追踪情绪是完全合情合理的。

sentences.en: My colleague, Dr. Gerilyn Hogg, and I have just recently begun research with a product called Spire, which measures your breath as a way of recording your stress level.
sentences.zh: 我的同事杰里琳·霍格博士和我最近刚刚开始一项关于一款名为Spire的产品的研究，该产品通过测量你的呼吸来记录你的压力水平。

sentences.en: And that's integrated back into your steps and onto your phone.
sentences.zh: 这会反馈到你的步数中并显示在你的手机上。

sentences.en: So it gives you indicators of are you moving and are you breathing and your relative stress level.
sentences.zh: 因此它能为你提供指标，告诉你你是否在运动、你是否在呼吸以及你的相对压力水平。

sentences.en: And that's just one of many applications and I think we're really at the forefront of these interesting applications that provide triggers to make behavior change.
sentences.zh: 这只是众多应用中的一个，我认为我们确实正处于这些有趣的应用程序的前沿，它们能提供触发机制来促成行为改变。

sentences.en: Do you think psychologists could use apps like these when looking for ways to help their clients?
sentences.zh: 您认为心理学家在寻找帮助客户的方法时可以使用这些应用程序吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if that's anything that you study, but I'm just curious as to where do you take this knowledge?
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否是您研究的内容，但我只是好奇您会将这些知识运用于何处？

sentences.en: Well, I think you can take the knowledge a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为你可以从很多方面运用这些知识。

sentences.en: I mean, one is that it's very individually empowering.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一方面，它对个人有很强的赋能作用。

sentences.en: So people have now a new tool in their own arsenal to make change on their own behalf.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们现在自己的武器库中多了一项新工具，可以为了自身的利益做出改变。

sentences.en: But it's also a very effective way to work with clinicians, coaches, and therapists.
sentences.zh: 但它也是与临床医生、教练和治疗师合作的一种非常有效的方式。

sentences.en: An application that I've been using is the Heart Lab or HeartMath, rather, which allows you to
sentences.zh: 我一直在使用的一个应用程序是Heart Lab，准确地说是HeartMath，它允许你

sentences.en: measure your heart rate in conjunction with your breathing as a mechanism for getting better mind-body coherence.
sentences.zh: 结合呼吸来测量心率，以此作为实现更好身心协调的机制。

sentences.en: So similar to meditation, but it's a way of showing your therapist the track record that you're keeping and she can then work with you on the mental triggers that are
sentences.zh: 因此，这类似于冥想，但它是一种向你的治疗师展示你一直在保持的记录的方式，然后她可以与你一起探讨那些

sentences.en: disrupting your thought patterns, causing you stress, causing you distress, and the things that actually improve that.
sentences.zh: 扰乱你的思维模式、给你带来压力、给你带来痛苦的心理触发因素，以及那些真正能改善这种情况的事情。

sentences.en: You've been a media psychologist for a while.
sentences.zh: 您担任媒体心理学家已经有一段时间了。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, with all this new technology is coming out, and it seems like it's coming out constantly, is it making your job more interesting,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，随着所有这些新技术的问世，而且看起来它们层出不穷，这是否让你的工作变得更有趣，

sentences.en: or what you're able to learn and use the technology?
sentences.zh: 或者让你能够学习和使用这些技术？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: It makes it fascinating, and it also makes it just, I'm absolutely able to justify the purchase of any piece of technology at
sentences.zh: 这让它变得非常迷人，而且也让我完全有理由购买任何科技产品，

sentences.en: all, because I just tell my husband, oh, honey, I have to study this.
sentences.zh: 因为我只需对丈夫说，哦，亲爱的，我必须研究这个。

sentences.en: But sure, it does two things.
sentences.zh: 但当然，它有两方面的作用。

sentences.en: One is that it keeps us very on the ball, because we're continually figuring out what are the affordances
sentences.zh: 一方面，它让我们保持高度敏锐，因为我们一直在弄清楚任何特定技术的赋能作用

sentences.en: or the attributes of any particular piece of technology, and how are we mapping that back to psychological theory?
sentences.zh: 或属性是什么，以及我们如何将这些映射回心理学理论？

sentences.en: Because as you know, it's not really about the tools.
sentences.zh: 因为如你所知，这其实与工具无关。

sentences.en: It's about human behavior and emotions and how we're wired.
sentences.zh: 这关乎人类的行为、情绪以及我们的天性。

sentences.en: And so if we understand those fundamentals, then we have the ability to evaluate all this new technology.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们了解了这些基础知识，我们就有能力评估所有这些新技术。

sentences.en: The bad thing is, every semester, I have to rewrite my syllabuses, because I need to keep the content up to date.
sentences.zh: 不好的一面是，每个学期我都必须重写教学大纲，因为我需要保持内容与时俱进。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Overall, and this is, you hear this often in the media, you know, there's a sense that social media and emerging technologies are changing
sentences.zh: 总的来说，你在媒体上经常听到这种说法，你知道，人们有一种感觉，即社交媒体和新兴技术正在改变

sentences.en: people, making them more narcissistic, self-involved.
sentences.zh: 人们，让他们变得更加自恋、以自我为中心。

sentences.en: You know, you said that you think they are making people more empathetic and responsible for other people's well-being.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你曾说过你认为它们实际上让人们更有同理心，对他人福祉更有责任感。

sentences.en: Can you explain why you think that?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下为什么你这么认为吗？

sentences.en: Can you give some examples?
sentences.zh: 你能举几个例子吗？

sentences.en: I believe that people are becoming more empathetic, because this connectivity and social media are allowing them to see other people globally in a
sentences.zh: 我相信人们正在变得更有同理心，因为这种连通性和社交媒体让他们能够在全球范围内看到其他人，

sentences.en: way that they've never been able to see before.
sentences.zh: 这是他们以前从未能够看到的。

sentences.en: I know a lot of people are worried about things like narcissism, but I think that's overstated.
sentences.zh: 我知道很多人担心自恋之类的事情，但我认为这被夸大了。

sentences.en: What is important is that people understand the benefits of technology and where they need to establish limits.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，人们要了解技术的益处以及他们需要在哪里建立限制。

sentences.en: You know, offline, we have all these patterns of behavior that we know how to take care of ourselves, self-care, but we now have to learn how to do this in this new environment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在线下，我们有各种各样的行为模式，我们知道如何照顾自己、进行自我关怀，但我们现在必须学会如何在这一新环境中做到这一点。

sentences.en: We have to extend our living space, so to speak, into the online arena.
sentences.zh: 可以说，我们必须将我们的生活空间扩展到在线领域。

sentences.en: So we have to learn how to set online boundaries.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须学会如何设定网络边界。

sentences.en: We have to learn how to respond to things.
sentences.zh: 我们必须学会如何对各种事情做出反应。

sentences.en: The Red Cross was able to raise five million dollars within 24 hours after the Haitian earthquake.
sentences.zh: 海地地震发生后，红十字会在24小时内筹集了五百万美元。

sentences.en: That's an extraordinary amount of participation.
sentences.zh: 这是一个了不起的参与度。

sentences.en: Now, while some people might have referred to that as slacktivism, saying that they're not really involved, the fact that people have
sentences.zh: 现在，虽然有些人可能会称之为“懒惰行动主义”（slacktivism），认为他们并没有真正参与，但人们拥有

sentences.en: that awareness that they were willing to participate in that small bit means that they're going to be much
sentences.zh: 这种意识并且愿意参与这一点微小的贡献，意味着他们对未来的呼吁会

sentences.en: more sensitive to future calls, so that they're aware of other people in need, and they'll be much more liable to help.
sentences.zh: 更加敏感，他们会意识到其他人有需要，并且更有可能伸出援手。

sentences.en: It also empowers the giver, because now there are all these kinds of ways where people can make a difference in very small ways.
sentences.zh: 这也赋予了捐赠者权力，因为现在有各种各样的方法可以让人们通过非常微小的方式产生影响。

sentences.en: That sense of agency is going to make people much more willing to participate.
sentences.zh: 这种主观能动性将使人们更加愿意参与。

sentences.en: So I think this idea that everyone has become totally self-focused is exactly wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为每个人都变得完全以自我为中心的这种观点是完全错误的。

sentences.en: So I think that we have a misconception of the dangers of technology.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为我们对技术的危险存在误解。

sentences.en: That's not to say there aren't probleMs. There are.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说不存在问题。确实存在。

sentences.en: It's important to have training, but we don't want to overstate the problems, because we don't want to miss the benefits, because there's tremendous upside.
sentences.zh: 进行培训很重要，但我们不想夸大问题，因为我们不想错过好处，因为这里有巨大的潜在优势。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Rutledge, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 好的，拉特利奇博士，非常感谢您做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: This was a fascinating conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是一次引人入胜的对话。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: For more information on Dr. Rutledge's work, and to hear more episodes, please go to our website,
sentences.zh: 有关拉特利奇博士工作的更多信息并收听更多单集，请访问我们的网站，

sentences.en: speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: speakingofpsychology.org.

sentences.en: With the American Psychological Association's Speaking of Psychology,
sentences.zh: 这里是美国心理学会的《心理学话语》，

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。
